result.rule: Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Attach to an activity boundary only these triggers: message, timer, escalation, conditional, signal, error, cancel, compensation or multiple. Never a none or link event.
When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.

result.rule: When the description states a specific activity or process-ending outcome: Label the corresponding BPMN activity or end event with a concise phrase that preserves the stated action or outcome; do not substitute a related action or add an unsupported one.

When the description states an activity with explicit alternatives or qualifiers that distinguish its scope: Label the corresponding BPMN element concisely while preserving those stated distinctions; do not generalize them away.

When the description states an activity together with criteria, optional supporting actions, or a later outcome associated with it: Label the BPMN task with a concise verb-object phrase for the activity itself. Keep associated criteria, alternatives, and subsequent outcomes out of the label unless they define the activity.

When the description states that an activity evaluates information and communicates a resulting outcome to another participant: Label the corresponding task to preserve both the evaluation and the communication, rather than naming only the communication.
